Contributing to WithinHostExperiment

Source: .github/CONTRIBUTING.md

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome at https://github.com/CuiweiG/WithinHostExperiment/issues. Please open pull requests against main.

The rest of this page records how changes move between GitHub and Bioconductor. The two sides use different names for the development branch, which is the easiest place to make a mistake.

Which branch a change goes to

Change GitHub branch Bioconductor branch Version
New features, changed defaults, refactoring, documentation for the next release main devel 1.1.z (odd y)
Bug fixes and documentation corrections for users of Bioconductor 3.24 RELEASE_3_24, after main RELEASE_3_24, after devel 1.0.z (even y)
  • GitHub main is Bioconductor devel. Bioconductor only builds devel and RELEASE_* branches, so every push to Bioconductor names the target explicitly: main:devel.
  • RELEASE_3_24 takes bug fixes and documentation corrections only. New features and changed defaults wait on main for Bioconductor 3.25 (spring 2027).
  • A bug fix goes into main first and is then cherry-picked to RELEASE_3_24. Each branch gets its own version bump.
  • When Bioconductor 3.25 is released, RELEASE_3_25 replaces RELEASE_3_24 as the branch for bug fixes, and RELEASE_3_24 is frozen.

Version numbers

Bioconductor uses x.y.z version numbers (https://contributions.bioconductor.org/versionnum.html):

  • y is odd on devel (1.1.z) and even on the release branch (1.0.z). The Bioconductor team changes y at each release; do not change x or y yourself.
  • Bump z in every commit that should reach users: 1.1.0 to 1.1.1 on devel, 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 on RELEASE_3_24. A pushed commit without a version bump is built, but not propagated: BiocManager::install() keeps serving the previous version.
  • Commits that only touch files left out of the package by .Rbuildignore (for example .github/) do not need a bump.
  • Builds run once a day and take about 24 hours, so a push appears on the build report (https://bioconductor.org/checkResults/) one or two days later. It reaches users once a build with the new version finishes without errors.

Remotes

This is the setup Bioconductor recommends (https://contributions.bioconductor.org/git-version-control.html):

git remote add upstream git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/WithinHostExperiment.git
git remote -v
# origin    https://github.com/CuiweiG/WithinHostExperiment.git (fetch)
# origin    https://github.com/CuiweiG/WithinHostExperiment.git (push)
# upstream  git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/WithinHostExperiment.git (fetch)
# upstream  git@git.bioconductor.org:packages/WithinHostExperiment.git (push)

ssh -T git@git.bioconductor.org info lists what the registered SSH key may read (R) and write (W); packages/WithinHostExperiment should show R W.

Pushing

Before committing, bring main up to date with Bioconductor. The Bioconductor team commits to devel too, for example the version bumps at each release:

git checkout main
git fetch upstream
git merge --ff-only upstream/devel

Devel (GitHub main to Bioconductor devel):

git push upstream main:devel
git push origin main

Release (the same name on both sides):

git fetch upstream
git checkout -b RELEASE_3_24 upstream/RELEASE_3_24   # first time only
git cherry-pick <commit on main>
# bump z in DESCRIPTION (1.0.0 to 1.0.1) and commit
git push upstream RELEASE_3_24
git push origin RELEASE_3_24

To push exactly the commit that was checked, push by hash:

git push upstream <hash>:refs/heads/devel
git push origin <hash>:refs/heads/main

Never force-push. Bioconductor does not accept rewritten history, and a GitHub ruleset blocks force-pushes and deletion on main and on RELEASE_* branches.

Continuous integration

The workflows in .github/workflows/ run on main with R-devel and on RELEASE_* branches with R 4.6 and Bioconductor 3.24: R CMD check on Linux, macOS and Windows, BiocCheckGitClone() and BiocCheck(), test coverage, and a check of citation(), links and spelling. The pkgdown site is built from main only. The versions are set at the top of each workflow; update them when Bioconductor 3.25 is released.
